articleTitle: Rational representation in spectrum conjugate domain for parameters determination of reflecting structures
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: An opportunity of use of rational representation in the spectrum conjugate domain for determination of parameters of reflecting structures using measured frequency reflection characteristics has been considered. An opportunity of use of the linear approaches for spectral data approximation by unipolar function and use of rational interpolation of the spectral data with the purpose of acceleration of a procedure of parameter determination of the additive exponential model has been considered. The properties of these methods and their comparison with analogous properties of other methods are presented.

articleTitle: The method of auxiliary sources in applied electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) with peculiarities, which could be considered to use it efficiently are introduce. The MAS was demonstrated as a suitable method for handling complex 2-D electromagnetic problems 111. The objective of this paper is to demonstrate his efiiciency to the 3-D Problems. Details of realization and results of solution particular problems are presented.

articleTitle: Modal basis method in radiation problems
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Genetical swarm optimization: a new hybrid evolutionary algorithm for electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: This paper presents a new hybrid evolutionary algorithm combining Particle Swarm Optimization and Genetic Algorithms, called GSO (Genetical Swarm Optimization). GSO algorithm is essentially a population-based heuristic search technique which can be used to solve combinatorial optimization problems, modeled on the concept of natural selection but also based on cultural and social evolution. Numerical results and comparison of the different techniques are presented for an electromagnetic optimization problem.

articleTitle: Fractional curl operator in reflection problems
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate some applications of the fractionalized curl operator in the scattering problems. Using the technique of fractionalizing a linear operator we obtain the presentation for the fractional curl operator for the functions of hvo variables expressed via exponents. We use ibis presentation in a plane wave reflection at oblique incidence on an impedance infinite surface. Applying fractional curl operator to a fired solution we obtain the fields that describe, in certain sense, an intermediate of "fractional" solution behveen the original solution and its dual solution. These "fractional" fields represent the solution of reflection problem from an anisotropic surface. The relation behveen the impedance of such an anisotropic surface and the original impedance are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Parametric representations of integral and pseudo-differential operators in diffraction problems
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Parametric representations of integral and pseudodifferential operators are used in the derivation of singular and hypersingular integral equations for a number of diffraction prnhlems. These equations can be solved numerically by the Method of Discrete Singularities, which has been completely grounded.

articleTitle: Semiasymptotic method for impedance plane with quasiperiodic spatial perturbation of parameters
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Effects of coupling of wave beam and surface wave at plane with spatially oscillating surface impedance are theoretically considered. Proposed method is asymptotic accordingly smoothness parameter and is numerical accordingly perturbation amplitudes. It combines advantages of the asymptotic and numeric methods in cases of quasiperiodic structures with large number of "periods". Obtained coupling coeficients are compared with known asymptotic expressions. Influence of number of spatial harmonic taking into account on solution errors is analyzed.

articleTitle: Using the method of minimum extension to extrapolation of antenna measurements
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Study of electromagnetic scattering by rain drops
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Communication performance demands ask for higher frequency bands, which are affected by precipitation. Particular attention should be devoted to the size of the particles, which are called hydrometeors such as rain (water drops), hail and snow [I]. This paper analyses the electromagnetic scattering by rain drops because train is the most important precipitation in our climatic conditions Rain consists of rain drops of various diameters from 0.01 to 0.7 cm and of various frequency (drop size distribution-DSD). The next problem is due to fact that water drops are created by material, which can be considered as lossy dielectric (exact series for scattering have been published as well [2], [3] and [4]). Therefore, both the reflected and transmitted wave should be analysed. That means that two various mechanisms creating the energetic losses of propagating electromagnetic wave exist. A part of energy is absorbed by water drops and the other part is scattered by water drops at various (also unwanted) directions. That creates several problems.

articleTitle: Transient wave beam diffraction by lossy dielectric half space
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: The mathematical models of problem about wave beams diffraction on a plane metallic grating
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper received mathematical models of paraxial wave beams scattering by strip gratings consisting of infinitely thin, for the solution of the Riemann-Hilbert problem method 11-21 and a method of singular integral equations 131 are used.

articleTitle: Fractional curl operator in radiation problems
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The fractional curl operator and its possible applications in electromagnetic problems are discussed. Specifically, we consider radiation from sheet and line current distributions. Applying fractionalized curl operator we obtain new "fractional" fields and corresponding "fractional" currents, and analyze their physical meanings. "Fractional" field can be considered as "intermediate" one between the original and dual fields. It can be treated as an extension of conventional duality principle. Expressions for the "fractional" fields and relation between "fractional" currents and the original currents are presented.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf analysis of the electromagnetic waves radiation from a circular waveguide cavity with an impedance termination: vector diffraction problem
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: 3D simulations of nanometric integrated optical circuits using surface plasmon polariton gap waveguide
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Nanometric optical waveguide can be made by using the dependence of surface plasmon polaritons on the gap-width between two parallel metallic plates. This waveguide can be called surface plasmon polariton gap-waveguide (SPGW). The H and E-plane closed-type and E-plane open-type optical circuits that consist of SPGWs have been considered. Three-dimensional numerical simulations have been performed for the nanometric optical circuits that consist of straight, branch and bend SPGWs. Results show that optical circuits considered in this paper can perform guiding, branching and bending function of optical waves in the nanometric device.

articleTitle: An analytical method of auxiliary sources solution for line source illumination of impedance cylinders
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: For a scattering problem with a circular impedance cylinder illuminated by a line source an analytical Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) solution has been derived. This may serve as B reference for the numerical MAS solution and comparisons between the analytical and numerical MAS solutions are presented. A very good agreement is found between the two MAS solutions with respect to excitation coefficients and mean boundary condition error for varying positions of the auxiliary sources and the Illuminating line source. This serves as a validation of the numerical MAS.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Investigation of EMI sensor orientation and position efefcts on buried metalic target discrimination [efefcts read effects]
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Near field ( ˜ 1 m) electromagnetic induction (EMI) sensing, from 10's of Hz up to 100's of kHz, has been successful in detecting subsurface metallic targets. However, the discrimination of buried unexploded ordinance (UXO) from innocuous objects still remains a challenging problem. The problem b more complicated in real field survey, when data are highly contaminated with noise and clutter. In EMI data the noise and clutter are generated from a sensor, surrounding media, sensor operation (motion and rotation) etc. Understanding and taking into account noises associated with the sensor motion and rotation are particularly important for identification and discrimination of actual UXO. To address these critical issues and to enhance of UXO identification, this paper investigates EMI scattering from a highly permeable and conducting objects subject to the state of the art of sensors using user friendly and freely available electromagnetic induction code based on the method of auxiliary sources [1]. At the end several numerical results are shown and analyzed to demonstrate the sensors rotation and shifting effects on EMI signals.

articleTitle: Monopole antenna calibration in GTEM cell
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Separated turnstile antenna on small LEO satellites
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Separated turnstile Antenna can provide saddle-shaped and hemispherical patterns. Its ability in making the arbitrary earth covering pattern has provided a lot of applications in small LEO satellites. In this article, the proper pattern for separated turnstile antenna which is mounted on a small LEO satellite, is synthesized and shaped. Wired model of separated turnstile antenna is analyzed by Moment Method and its gain pattern, polarization and input impedance are calculated. Ability of dual band operation of this antenna has been investigated in the paper and a dual band separated turnstile antenna bas been designed for the satellite. Also, Effects of antenna geometrical parameters on its pattern have been researched and calculated in the paper.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Iterative calculation method for two-dimensional model of reflector-type antenna with sharp nose radome
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: We consider a method of calculation of the radiation field of a two-dimensional reflector-type antenna in a radome, and of the scattered field if a plane electromagnetic wave is incident on radomeantenna system. The method is iterative, and based on solving the volume integral equation.

articleTitle: Matrix operator technique for analysis of wave transformers
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The matrix operator technique for modeling mode dinraction is presented. This approach was developed with B view to substantiate some modal expansion methods. It allows one to prove the correctness of matrix operator models and to investigate the convergence of approximate solutions analytically. In this paper, the technique is applied to the analysis of two-port wave transformers. The developed models have the form of Cayley's transform of operator matrices. The approach can be useful for analytic-numerical solution of various electromagnetic problems.

articleTitle: Method of impedance analogue of electromagnetic space at research of dispersion of electromagnetic waves from nonuniform plasma in Tokamak T-10
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Analysis of the electric field distribution on perfectly conducting wing sections by application of a conformal mapping
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Design and realization of printed LPDA at UHF band
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Simulation of aerial, ground and subsurface object scattering characteristics
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Numerical methods for calculating radar scattering from complex shape objects (with surface breaks), placed in free space, above and under the ground interface are presented. For aerial and ground perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) objects, wholly or partly covered with radio absorbing materials have been developed asymptotical (for electrically large sizes of objects) method. Numerical method, based on surface integral equations for scattering by subsurface PEC and dielectric objects of Rayleigh or resonance sizes, is proposed. The scattering by reflector antenna and antenna system with ogive nose radome are considered also. Radar cross section (RCS) results for cruise missile, aircrafts, tanks are demonstrated. As well the results of subsurface mine-like objects scattering at monochromatic and pulse incidence are shown.

articleTitle: MDS modeling of pre-fractal printed antennas
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper new method for modeling of planar antennas is presented. Finite order Sierpinski carpet antennas are considered. Diffraction problem is reduced to hypresingular integral equation. This equation is solved using the Method of Discrete Singnlarities (MDS). Some of obtained numerical results are presented.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a dual-band quadrifilar helix antenna
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: This paper presents a simple and innovative method for designing and optimizing a QHA antenna for dual-hand operation. The substantial point is the use of a very simple impedance matching network at both frequency hands to omit the reactance parts, which makes the overall optimization simpler. This antenna is to be implemented on the Asian Small Multi-Mission Satellite (SMMS).

articleTitle: Implementation of phase retrieval techniques for improving the results of phased array antennas near-field measurements
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Reciprocity principle and electromagnetic wave scattering by plano-chiral double-periodic array
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The vector relation of field amplitudes of direct and reversed scenarios of wave diffraction by double-periodic array is derived from the Lorenz lemma. The hiorthogonality of polarization eigenstates of wave propagated in direct and reversed direction in wave channel formed by incident wave and diffraction order is shown. The facility of essential difference of polarization transforms at direct and reversed propagation in wave channel is established for the instance of planar chiral array.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic interaction of a nonmonochromatic field and a moderately orthotropic composite material with a dielectric surface coat
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: For a moderately orthotropic composite material with a dielectric surface coat and an nonmonochromatic field source of arbitrary plane shape general mathematical expressions of vectorpotential components are obtained with a help of two-side Laplace transformation.

articleTitle: The problems of electromagnetic waves diffraction on the dielectric index step in the waveguides with metallic bounds
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Symmetry classes of lasing modes in two nanospaced microdisks
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: We present a data on the spectra and thresholds of two optically coupled microdisk lasers. The study is based on the reduction of the 3D lasing eigenvalue problem to a 2D one, through the effective index approximation. The latter problem is formulated in rigorous manner for Maxwell's equations with transmission boundary conditions at the disk boundaries and the radiation condition at infinity.

articleTitle: A new method for the computation of eigenmodes in dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Equations of electrodynamics with nonequilibrium fluctuations in many component hydrodynamic medium
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Closed system of equations for electromagnetic field and hydrodynamic medium (many component plasma) has been obtained taking into account binary fluctuations ofthe field. Statistical operator of the system was found on the base of the Bogolyubov reduced description method and quasirelativistic quantum electrodynamics. Calculations were carried ont in the Hamilton gauge up to the second order of a perturbation theory in interaction or the first order in gradients.

articleTitle: Some new statements of inverse problems of recognition
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The inverse problems are examined the solutions of which can are reduced to the solution of the integral equation of the first kind with an inexact kernel and inexact right part. Such inverse problems sometimes are called as problems of recognition [I, 21. In some cases the solution of such problems is senseless in traditional statement [3,4]. In the given work two new statements of inverse problem of recognition are offered. The possible method of their solutions that is based on Tikhonov's method regularization with a choice of special mathematical models of researched process is suggested. The questions of existence and stability of the approximate solutions to the small variations of the initial data are considered here. The opportunities of the specified statements are demonstrated on test examples.

articleTitle: Simulation and solution of the inverse problem of atmospheric turbulence measurements computation in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: The electrodynamical model of decameter radiochannel with isotropic receiving-transmitting antennas
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Beam shaping of turnstile antenna for LEO satellite with genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to create a link with a flat received signal level, which is not depend on elevation angle between LEO satellite and earth receivers. This problem is solved using beam shaping of separated turnstile antenna for satellite employing a real coded Genetic Algorithm (CA). We have Introduced a special strategy to improve the results of the algorithm using the concept of derivation in cost function (CF).

articleTitle: Modificated Fresnel antenna
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The general approach to analysis of sounded Fresnel antenna is considered. The frequency characteristics of Fresnel antenna are analyzed. The radiation characteristics of Fresnel antenna are considered. The influence of reflector in Fresnel antenna is considered.

articleTitle: Large flat plate models in the physical optics method for RCS calculations
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The calculation of Radar Cross Section (RCS) of arbitrarily large perfectly conducting body is presented. The body is modelled as triangular meshes of any size by the help of graphical tools. For the calculation of scattered field, Physical Optics(P0) surface integral is analytically evaluated over each of the triangular meshes. Due to the analytical integration, there is no limitation on the size of the triangles.

articleTitle: Global optical and wireless networking - emerging opportunities for electromagnetic research
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of liquid crystal devices
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Mathematical modeling of liquid crystal (LC) devices is demonstrated through LC directors' reorientation and electro-optical modeling. For director distribution simulation, 3-D finite difference and finite element methods have been developed. In optical simulation, a new derivation of extended Jones matrix is given. Besides, research has demonstrated that the evolutionary algorithms (EA) can yield robust globally optimized solutions. Application examples using the modeling and optimization methods to design LCDs will also be presented.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: The calculation of structure inhomogeneity influence on eddy currents value in armor composite material
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: By a different approximation of the integral of Bessel’s functions product the accuracy of known method of an eddy cnrrents density calculation has increased. Besides the conditions have created for the representation of an eddy currents decrement, that is caused by structure inhomogeneity with the help of elementary functions only. The linearization of an obtained approximating dependence supplies the engineering calculation method of eddy currents decrement as a function of the effective sizes of the surface model crack, of the generalised parameter of transducer and of dielectric surface coat depth in armor composite material.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Convergence of the Galerkin method for numerical calculation of the guided modes of an integrated optical guide
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Comparison of two neural network optimization approaches
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: This paper compares two optimization methods for training Neural Networks: the typical supervised feed-forward hackpropagation algorithm and an improved Particle Swarm Optimization method. The aim is to highlight advantages and drawbacks of these techniques in order to suitably apply them to electromagnetic problems. Some numerical results and comparisons are presented analyzing a load forecasting problem. Neural Networks are trained for a particular power system load consuption signal, for future time prediction.

articleTitle: Fast integral equation techniques for propagation problems
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper, the Method of Moments (MOM) solution is achieved for scattering problems by using the stationary Spectrally Accelerated Forward-Backward method (FBSA) and the non-stationary Spectrally Accelerated BiConjugate Gradient Stabilized (SA-BiCGSTAB) method, with a storage requirement and a computational cost of O(N) per iteration where N is the number of surface unknowns in the discretized integral equation. The SA-BiCGSTAB method is applied over rough terrain profdes as well as reentrant surfaces which can not be handled by any conventional stationary iterative technique.

articleTitle: Near fields aperture antennas measurements by means of a controllable microstrip reflectarray
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper design of the measuring set for antennas measurements based on the the reflective type antenna array are considered. Reflectarray is executed on the basis of microstrip dipoles. In structure of each printed dipole of the reflective type antenna array is present controllable microwave element. Changing conductivity of such element, we can effectively operate by length of a printed dipole of the reflective type antenna array. At the same time change of a dipole length results to essential variation of it's radar cross-section. Thus, there is an opportunity in the electric way to change a place of the greatest reflection from the reflective type antenna. This circumstance enables to measure a near fleld of the researched antenna. It is obvious, that the most convenient for such researches appeared aperture aerials. Microstrip reflectarrays because of their high adaptability to manufacture appeared the most convenient tool in such near field antennas measurements.

articleTitle: The effects of frequency dependent soil parameters and incident wave polarizations on GPR performance
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The effects of the electromagnetic properties of soil, such as permittivity and permeability as a function of frequency, on the performance of Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is presented, both in time and frequency domains. The incident wave is assumed to be the Gaussian pulse, which is then transformed to frequency-domain by means of the Fourier Transform. Using the frequency dependent parameters of the soil and different polarizations for the incident wave, the transmitted wave to ground and the reflected signal from its surface are obtained in frequency domain, and then transformed back to the time domain. The method is rigorous in the seuse that no approximation is made in the simulation, and better results are obtained in comparison with the available data from other researchers. The choice of the incident wave polarization for some applications is also discussed.

articleTitle: Electron trajectories in model of longitudinally varying magnetic field
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The theoretical analysis of electron motion in longitudinally varying magnetic field of MPFS is given in this paper. We offered the focusing mechanism of electrons in such systems based on this analysis. We investigate the influence of elctron inlet conditions on a character of electron trajectory in MPFS that consists of both only SmCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> washers and alternating SmCo<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> and NdFeB wahers. Theoretical calculations are in good agreement with experimental research of electron trajectory of non relativistic beam placed in such MPFS.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of a cavity gyrotron on the basis of hypersingular integral equations
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Hypersingular integral equation (HSIE) for a coaxial gyrotron full wave analysis is derived in case of TM waves. Considered electrodynamic problem is a problem to find nontrivial solutions for homogenous Maxwell equations. It reduced to a problem of the first kind for a two-dimensional Helmholtz equation for electric Borgnis function in cross-section of a cavity gyrotron. Derived HSIE can be solved numerically using a method of discrete singularities and special quadrature formulas of the interpolative type.

articleTitle: Parameters of the lower ionosphere inferred from night-time VLF atmospherics
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modelling of cylindrically conformal array antennas
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: An excitation problem for a cylindrical microstrip phased array antenna Is discussed. The array consists of N periodically arranged elements. Each element represents a sub-array of M patches. Each patch Is fed by a probe which is introduced in a line charge approximation. The Integral equation for finding the patch surface currents Is formulated and solved in the spatial domain by the moment method. The far field is calculated io a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Some generalizations for the synthesis problem of the waveguide antenna array
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The problem of formation of the prescribed amplitude radiation pattern is considered with an additional condition of restriction on the value of electromagnetic field in a near zone. Variational statement of the synthesis problem allows to satisfy simultaneously the putted requirements to the amplitude radiation pattern and to take into account restrictions on the sought excitation factors of waveguide array. Use of weight functions and weight multiplier in criterion of optimization enables to regularize a degree of satisfaction of requirements to the radiation pattern, factors of excitation, as well as the values of electromagnetic field in the given areas of a near zone. The expressions for the both radiation pattern and the field in a near zone are received in an operational form for convenience of solving the synthesis problem that substantially facilitates this process.

articleTitle: Nonlinear transition radiation of the radially restricted modulated electron beam from the sharp vacuum-plasma border
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Electromagnetic field of the radially restricted electron beam normally falling from vacuum on the sharp border of isotropic plasma is considered in quadratic nonlinear approach. Such a fleld consists of the transition radiation second harmonic, mixed harmonic between the radiation and electron beam eigeufield and the quasi-stationary electric field.

articleTitle: On reflection and refraction of the electromagnetic waves on the linear and nonlinear media interface
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The method of the auxiliary Cauchy problem for the Maxwell equations is used to solve the scalar problem on the fall of the plane wave on the linear and nonlinear media interface. The necessary and sufficient conditions on the traces of the Cauchy problems solutions in the upper and lower semi-spaces are obtained in terms of the Fourier transforms. The initial problem is reduced to algebraic system of equations consisting of these relations and fields conjunction condition on the media interface.

articleTitle: An analysis method and application for a simple loaded loop antenna
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Toward nonstationary excitation theory in computational electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: The use of projection methods for numerical solution of electromagnetic wave diffraction problems
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The elaboration of direct Computational methods for efficient and fast modelling of problems of diffraction from locally inhomogeneous bodies is a topical problem in the development of modern numerical methods. Methods based on projection procedures are considered in this paper in the case Of linear operator equations. Projection methods applied to calculate the electromagnetic field distribution involve discrete models, which can be obtained when the radiation conditions at infinity are algorithmically taken into account. Note that these conditions are not local with any formulation. The radiation conditions are linear limitations coupling field values at aU points of the space, or these conditions are formulated via the Maxwell equations as linear relationships for the electromagnetic field components on any closed surface in a homogeneous space. The second peculiarity of electromagnetic diffraction problems is the fundamental energetic nonclosedness of a system. Energy comes from the exterior ofthe system, and most of it goes to infinity. Diffraction problems involve operator equations that are not sign-determined in any . functional space. Therefore, it becomes necessary to develop computational methods for solving linear nonself-conjugate boundary value problems. At the same time, diffraction problems are similar to elementary problems for well-known processes in the field theory. This allows one to hope that universal and efficient algorithms of solving diffraction problems can he developed.

articleTitle: Fifth-harmonic pealung ESB class-F amplifier
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The paper presents design and simulation of microwave class-F power amplifier based on the ESB microstrip structure with doubleperiod holes at the ground plane. Proposed structure allows to provide high amplifier efficiency within wide frequency hand.

articleTitle: Open-cell layer estimate for scattering from impedance cylinders
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Recently, a new approximation of a layer surrounding the scatterer and not reflecting outgoing waves was proposed and employed for computing the scattering from convex conducting cylinders. Here this technique is applied to impedance structures. The layer consists of cells and placed on the scattering surface. Inside each cell, the field scattered is expended in terms of waves propagating from the cell sides except the outer one. The realizability and appropriateness of the construction are checked by solving the scattering from circular and rectangular impedance cylinders. The approach takes advantage of simplicity and provides sufficiently accurate results in wide range of frequencies.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering characteristics of aerial and ground radar objects
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Scattering characteristics for series of aerial and ground objects are considered. Evaluation of these characteristics based on calculation method for perfectly conducting electrically large objects (possibly placed near ground) wholly or partly covered by absorbing coating. Also we propose analysis of obtained numerical results.

articleTitle: Field focusing in the presence of the metamaterial plate
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Green function study of the non-stationary polaritonic response of a two-dimensional excitonic layer
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: MDS analysis of electrically large dual-reflector "PACO" antenna in 2-D
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this work, Method of Discrete Singularities (MDS) is applied for a full numerical analysis of two-dimensional (2-D) model of dual-reflector PACO (parabolic subreflector and conical reflector) antenna, for the both polarization cases. Numerical results are shown, to illustrate the performance of the considered antenna.

articleTitle: Plane wave diffraction by a 3D special slotted cone
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The plane wave diffraction problem for a 3D special slotted conical structure is considered. The structure under consideration is a semi-infinite circular perfectly conducting cone with longitudinal slots and an isotropic one inside. Studying the plane wave diffraction by such a structure is a canonical problem. By virtue the method that is based on using the Kontorovich-Lehedev integral transforms and the semi-inversion method the electromagnetic problem is reduced to solving a system of linear algebraic equations for Fourie coefficients of scattered fields. The numerical algorithm for solving this system is constructed. Field behavior near the surface singularities and field in the wave zone are presented.

articleTitle: Analytical study of properties of layered periodic methamaterials
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Simulation of spectroscopic ellipsometry for dielectric lamellar gratings
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Spectroscopic ellipsometry for lamellar gratings made of lossless dielectric materials is numerically investigated by using the rigorous coupled-wave formulation based on Li’s Fourier factorization rules. Accurate values of the ellipsometric angles are obtained with small number of Fourier components, and it is shown that accurate estimation of the grating parameters is possible in reasonable computation time.

articleTitle: Quasioptical beamshaping utilizing analytical gradients
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: A general synthesis method is proposed for the computation of quasioptical beamshapers. The method is based on the derivation of an analytical expmsion for the gradient to a predefined target functional. Using gradient information, a variable metric method for instance can be used to optimize the functional. The efficiency of the method is demonstrated in two examples; Fourier Gratings and a dual-offset configuration of reflectors are designed as quasioptical beamsplitters, respectively.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of a leaky-wave antenna with a reflection grating of finite extent
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Accurate two-dimensional mathematical model of the scattering of the natural electric-type guided modes of a slab dielectric waveguide from the finite number of rectangular grooves cut in the perfectly electric conducting (PEC) screen is built. A narrow beam with sidelobe level 2OdB is optimized with the aid of genetic algorithm. Application to leaky-wave antennas is discussed.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Scattering-matrix approach for modeling of electromagnetic response of plasmons in a grid-gated double-quantum-well field-effect transistor
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The terahertz (THz) absorption spectra of plasmon modes in a grid-gated double-quantum-well (DQW) field-effect transistor VET) structure is analyzed theoretically and numerically using the scattering matrix approach and is shown to faithfully reproduce strong resonant features of recent .experimental observations of THz photoconductivity in such a structure.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling of frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The problem of plane electromagnetic wave diffraction by a multilayer planar frequency selective surface has been solved in the paper. Integral equations for the problem had been formulated in both spectral and spatial domain: The integral equations had been solved by the Galerkin method with entire domain basis functions taking into account the edge condition. Regularization techniques for matrix equations resulting from integral equations in both spectral and spatial domain have been suggested in the paper.

articleTitle: Whispering and wave guiding properties of periodic structures
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: It has been shown that periodical structures always possess guiding and whispering properties. The existence criterion for all types of guiding and whispering modes has been found. The dependence of guiding frequency on the geometrical parameters of structures and the fine structure of continuous spectra of self-adjoint extension of Laplace operator has been investigated. Approximate expressions for the lower guiding frequencies have been derived [I-31.

articleTitle: The method for S-matrix calculation of arbitrary three dimensional waveguide's insertions
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: We developed a physico-mathematical model describing the excitation and the distribution of electromagnetic waves in an anisotropic waveguide in the three-dimensional case. In this paper, the finite difference technique is applied to the waveguide discontinuity problem for the scattering matrix parameter computation. The results of calculating of the scattering coeflicieut of the main mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of the elettromagnetic field and scattering of a slot antenna through hibrid 2D Wiener-Hopf technique and method of moment
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present an effective analytical approach in order to perform the analysis of the electromagnetic performance of a slot antenna. In this paper the main idea is to show how it is possible to get a closed form solution of the considered problem through the development ofa general analytical approach that let us consider the possible presence of any kind of linear stratified structure as loading medium in the shielded volume. In order to do that the double spatial Fourier transform is introduced, leading to a suitable formalism in the spectral domain rephrasing the electromagnetic problem in an equivalent circuit network model problem. The circuit network approach in the spectral domain yields a sort of Wiener-Hopf equation that can he analytically solved, through a suitable extended version of the Wiener-Hopf approach, or numerically faced and interactively solved with the requested accuracy through the Method of Moments in the spectral domain.

articleTitle: Application of genetic algorithms for optimization of a FSS reflectarray antenna
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper we describe the design and optimization of a reflectarray antenna with an offset feed. The reflectarmy is formed by a layer of frequency selective surface (FSS), e.g., a gangbuster surface above the ground plane. Phase synthesis on the reflectarray surface is achieved by varying local geometry of the FSS layer. Genetic Algorithm is used to shape the far field radiation pattern io the broadside direction and to reduce level of side lobes.

articleTitle: Properties of cascade-connected partially absorbing and reflecting waveguide resonators
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Differintegral /spl alpha/-/spl Omega/-forms of charges and currents distribution on the fractal artificial media
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Geometrical and physical aspects of differintegral forms application for simulation of fractal layer of charges and currents distribution in artificial medium is considered. Potentials of fractal fiber are applied to simulation of electromagnetic problems solutions in areas with varied charges and currents topology.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Spin polarization of electron current in semimagnetic semiconductor nanostructures
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The influence of an external constant magnetic field ou the voltage-current characteristics and spin polarization coeffrcient of the electron current in a double-harrier resonant-tunneling nanostructures composed of semimagnetic semiconductor layers has beeu investigated.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The use of the traditional optical pyrometry methods in the temperature diagnostics problem of the dusty plasma jets, which are characterized by structured complexity and transience, is limited. Stability of the parameter estimation procedure of the motion of the hvo-phase gas-dispersible ambiences, on essences presenting itself ill-posed inverse problem [l], depends on the data accuracy and equation structure, which must be corresponding with the measurement hardware realization.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Photon blockade of light in an interface between a metal film and a nonlinear medium
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The theoretical investigation of nonlinear surface polariton excitation in the metal fdm, contacting with the nonlinear medium in one side and the linear medium io other side is presented. We consider that the nonlinear surface polariton excitation occurs due to the light falling on the metal film from linear medium with the incident angle greater that the total internal reflection angle. The phenomena of photon blockade and optical histahility are predicted.

articleTitle: Dyadic Green's function for radialy layered cylindrical waveguides
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Dyadic Green's Functions (DGF) for cylindrical dielectric stratified media has been calculated. A cylindrical two-layered stratitled waveguide is considered as the geometry under investigation. Similar to other stratified problems; the method of scattering superposition is used to calculate the DGF for the structure in terms of cylindrical vector wave functions.

articleTitle: A new hybrid FDTD field-teleportation approach for modeling radiating/scattering structures
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The essence of the technique, called Field Teleportation, is to invoke the principle of equivalent sources (Schelkunoff's currents) using FDTD's discrete definition of the curl to copy any field propagating in one FDTD domain to a finite region of another domain without distortion [1]. Here an approach to teleport a frequency domain field into FDTD domain has been successfully tested for realistic large objeet scattering problem. The teleported field is used in FDTD to illuminate a scattering object introduced into the test region and the time-domain scattered signal has been transformed back into the frequency domain as induced equivalent surface currents. Having these currents, calculation of the farfield scattering becomes a trivial procedure. For the case of an exact frequency-domain solution, the error introduced by field-teleportation for 5λ 5λ by 2λ modeled space with PEC boundary is less than -110 dB and the phase error is less than 0.16 degree. For the case of field obtained by Uuiform Theory of Diffraction (UTD) on condense grid, intrinsic error has not exceeded -60 dB in magnitnde and ±3 degree in phase. In this case main e m r caused by H-field retrieving from E-field on condensed (non-Yee) grid. Our modeling shows high importance of the grid matching between any frequency domain method and FDTD (E and H-field components have to he found on Yee-grid for the hest field teleportation).

articleTitle: Eigenmodes and resonant frequencies of multi-laver and multi-strip planar structures
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The numerical-analytical approach was developed for analysis of various multi-layer and multi-strip resonant and periodical planar structures. Shown, that approach has high accuracy and requires small computer resources.

articleTitle: Use of plane wave decomposition for the estimation error analysis in microwave introscopy
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Representation of radiation field of microwave iotroscopy measurement unit in form of wave beam was considered. Allocation of the reflected field and reflection coefficient has been calculated using simple expressions for evaluation of reflection of each plane wave of decomposition. Magnitude of deviations of Fresnel coefficient estimations used in microwave introscopy from its values calculated with use of the wave beam has been considered. Reflection characteristics for various values of sue of the radiating aperture and the reflector, location of structures under test have been obtained.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: The effective index of optical waveguide based on finite difference beam propagation method
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper a new method based on Finite Difference Beam Propagation Method (FD-BPM) is presented to find the effective index of different kinds of optical waveguides. In the first step, we use FD-BPM for the general optical waveguide (Fig.]) which is excited with a Gaussian pulse. In the second step, we trace the propagation of the wave along the waveguide. After some steps, the wave could be decomposed into a set of modes. For each of these modes we compute its energy in all 9 regions of space in order to distinguish the modes that could be propagated. Finally we sweep the frequency and for each frequency we compute the effective index for each mode by using the stored energy in each region. In this way the relation between the stored energy and the effective index is formulated. To verify the developed method and its applicability, the derived equations and computed numerical results are compared with published results available for rib-waveguide and ridged waveguide. A good agreement in each case is found.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves described in terms of the zeros of their far-zone patterns
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Two-dimensional electromagnetic waves are discussed by means of the location of zeros of far. zone patterns on the complex plane Examples are given for the case when the scatterers are made of polygonal cylindem It is shown that contributions of scattering from the edges of the obstacles are well described by the infhite sequences of zeros that lead to idnity on the complex plane. The locations and directions of infinite sequences are closely related to the edge shapes in real space, so that the edge effects in high frequency scheme can he studied from geometrical considerations of these zeros.

articleTitle: Modeling of the LF-MF radiowave propagation over inhomogeneous irregular radiopaths
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: A method of calculation of an attenuation function of the ground wave field by means of generalized Feinherg’s equation taking into account the terrain relief is considered. It is possible to calculate the electromagnetic field in the LF-MF range over extensive inhomogeneous paths with a "had" conductivity. The attenuation function is calculated on a model of a plane Earth's surface on the first part of the path. Predicting maps of geoelectric sections and topographical digital maps characterizing the terrain relief and different types of forests are the basis for attenuation function calculations.

articleTitle: Surface currents induced by the E-polarized wave on curvilinear strips
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The problem of scattering of the E-polarized electromagnetic wave by cylindrical curvilinear strip is considered. The cross-section of the strip is an arc of a smooth curve. The problem is reduced to a singular integral equation (SIE) of the first kind with respect to surface currents' density. The SIE is convenient both for application of direct numerical method (mechanical quadratures) and for its transformation to a second kind's integral equation by the Vekua-Carleman's method of regularization. A large class of guide arcs for the cylindrical strips is examined. It includes some simple parabolic arcs where the limit passage to rectilinear segment is possible (important for testing) and rather difficult arcs that have many turning points. Except for common dynamic model of the problem the quasistatic model (it supposes a simple explicit solution) is presented. The comparison of numerical results of calculations by the indicated methods for the models is carried out.

articleTitle: On the designing of effective calculation algorithm for shielded multiconductor transmission lines
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: For the purpouse of designing of effective and universal calculation algorithm of the shielded multiconductor transmission lines parameters existing now rigorous methods of boundary value problems solutions are considered. At low frequencies the most preferred is the method of discrete singularities. A calculation algorithm of electromagnetic fields and dispersion characteristics of shielded multiconductor transmission lines based on mode matching method and recalculation formulas is suggested.

articleTitle: The measuring of structure inhomogeneity sizes in armor composite materials by two-dimensional processing of scanning data
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Excitation of hemispherical dielectric resonator by radial magnetic dipole
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The excitation is studied of electromagnetic oscillations by a radial magnetic dipole in a dielectric hemisphere placed on ideally conductive flat surface. The amplitude resonance is observed in frequency spectrum when source dipole frequency approaches that of eigen oscillation of resonator. The excitation becomes more effective when the magnetic dipole is placed in the maximum of appropriate mode of resonator.

articleTitle: Mathematical modeling and simulation of backscattering from hydrometeors of different types
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Non-linear acoustic oscillations in a strongly inhomogeneous medium
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Advantages of doublet modes for high-power millimeter-wave generation
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The application in vacuum electron oscillators of degenerated modes, which are split due to absence of the exact symmetry of oscillatory circuits, is considered. General peculiarities of the interaction of electron flows with such modes are described. The spatial-harmonic magnetron oscillator is used as a practical example of the study. It is shown that the usage of doublet modes weaken size restrictions on the oscillator cavity design, can provide higher values of the device efficiency, as in spatial-harmonic maimeter-wave magnetrons, or a wide range of frequency tuning, like in the case of clinotrons.

articleTitle: Backscattering from rain: mathematical models
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Automated design of corrugated conical horns for dual-band applications
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: A highly efficient full-wave model and CAD of conical corrugated horns is discussed. The capabilities of the CAD tools are demonstrated by the design of dual-hand horn operating over the 20 - 21.5 and 29.5 - 31.5 GHz bands. A comparison of the designed horn characteristics obtained with the Kirchhoff-Huygens approach and Wiener-Hopf technique is presented.

articleTitle: Modeling of stochastic processes in gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: This article reviews theoretical studies on stochastic processes in gyrotrons. Three different types of stochasticity related to gyrotron operation are considered. First, stochasticity in electron residual energies may develop at the resonator exit. Second, stochastic temporal radio-frequency oscillations can set in. Third, the high-frequency field structure can exhibit spatial chaos in the azimuthal direction.

articleTitle: Surface plasmon polaritons on nanostructured surfaces and thin films
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Surface plasmon polariton behaviour on periodically nanostructured metal surfaces and thin films is discussed. Such metallic nanostructures act as polaritonic crystals for surface polaritons, in analogy to photonic crystals for light waves. In this paper surface polariton Bloch mode spectrum on the structured surfaces and films is overviewed and manifestations of various surface plasmon modes in the optical properties of metallic nanostrnctures are considered. Surface plasmon polaritons me emerging as a new optical information carrier that enables signal manipulation and processing on the subwavelength scale and development of integrated photonic circuits.

articleTitle: Whistler wave emission by a modulated electron beam on a metal-plasma boundary: near-field region
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Transition and Cherenkov radiation in the near-fieid region of the thin radially restricted modulated electron beam injected to the plasma from the conductive plane along the magnetic fieid were calculated. It has been shown that the length of the wave excited by transition mechanism in the presence of constant magnetic field increases when plasma density decreases. The length of the wave excited on the second and third harmonics by Cherenkov mechanism decreases with the increasing of plasma density and beam modulation frequency. The obtained results are in a good agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering on irregular imperfectly conducting structures
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Two electromagnetic scattering problems for irregular imperfectly conducting structures are considered. The first one is harmonic dipole field scattering on a bicone at which approximate boundary conditions are fulfilled. The bicone consists of two infinite cones with different surface properties (resistive shells) those depend on distance from vertexes. The other problem is devoted to studying electromagnetic scattering on 3D System of plane angular resistive sectors. Analytical and numerical solutions are obtained. Effects of resistivity are analyzed.

articleTitle: A wavelet-based approach to analyze the electromagnetic wave effects on microwave transistors
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: A new wavelet-based simulation approach for the analysis and simulation of microwavelmm-wave transistors is presented. The Daubechies-base wavelet approach is applied to semiconductor equations to generate a nonuniform mesh. This allows forming fine and coarse grids in locations where variable solutions change rapidly and slowly, respectively. Also, some modifications for using the generated nonuniform mesh, which has been obtained based on the dc solution, in the ac analysis is presented.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic analysis of the near field for 2D and 3D metal bodies
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper, the solution of the second kind integral equation for the surface current density is used for the mathematical modeling of the near field. The transformation of the integral equation is realized for metallic polyhedron bodies. Though, the kernel of the integral equation is not singular, the convergence of the computational solution can be improved by the analytic transformation of the equation kernel. The solution of the integral equation is found by the collocation method and the Galerkin method with the trigonometric basis. The comparison of the results obtained by these methods is presented. As it is shown, a better accuracy of the numerical integration using the collocation method is realized by the method of rectangles.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of two-dimensional backward wave meta-material based on parallel-plate waveguide filled with double ring resonators
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Integral transforms in time-domain problems for unclosed conical surfaces
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics of plasma oscillations in semiconductor microdevices with two-dimensional electron channels
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Electromagnetic theory of plasma oscillations in field-effect transistor with two-dimensional electron channel is presented. Two different key electromagnetic problems are considered. They are the problems of diffraction of the plane electromagnetic wave (i) on the slot in infinite perfectly conductive plane, which is bridged by 2D electron channel and (ii) on the perfectly conductive strip, which screens partially an infinite 2D electron sheet located at a given distance from the strip. New physics inherent in these problems is revealed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the 2D nonconcentric large reflector antenna-in-radome system: H-polarization case
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: 2D nonconcentric reflector antenna-in-radome system is analyzed for H-polarization case. Rigorous formulation is performed depending on the MOR, Green's function and CSP methods. Larger geometries are solved in reasonable cpu times by using the FFT based algorithm in the computation of the Green's function.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave diffraction by flat semi-infinite strip grating
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The electromagnetic (EM) wave reflection by a flat semi-infinite grating (SIG) of metal strips is studied using the operator method. The full-wave specral method is applied for the key problem of diffraction by a single strip. The nonlinear equation is termas of the operator of reflection from SIG has been built. The anlytic form of reflected field in the case of the plane wave incidence and thin SIG has been built. The analytic form of reflected field in the cases of the plane wave incidence and thin SIG of narrow strips has been obtained by the steepest-descent method. This solution is anylysed from the physical point of view and compared with alternative accurate integral representation of field reflected from thin SIG.

articleTitle: Diffraction of a short pulse by a slot in an impedance screen
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave diffraction by the microstrip two-periodic grating of chiral metal strips
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Reflection characteristics of microstrip two-periodic gratings of perfectly conducting infinitely long strips having the complex shape are considered. The effect when reflected field possess orthogonal polarization relative to incidence wave polarization is considered. The possibility of insertion the control device in strips for the transformation considered grating to the array from the strip disconnected elements is proposed. The possibility for the structure application as high-impedance surface is considered. The comparison of the reflection properties of the two-periodic gratings of non-chiral strips and straight-line strip gratings is presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering by a smooth imperfectly conducting cylindrical obstacle
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: New strong in mathematical sense and numerically efficient method for investigation of two-dimensional boundary value problem of electromagnetic wave diffraction by infinite and homogeneous in longitudinal direction imperfectly conductive cylinder of arbitrary smooth cross section is suggested. The imperfect conductivity is modelled by the bounday condition of the third kind, for example, by Leontovich condition with impedance, which is supposed to be an arbitrary smooth function ofpoints of the obstacle cross section contour.

articleTitle: Surface wave excitation by a waveguide aperture with an impedance flange
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper, the theoretical analysis of energy characteristics and radiation patterns of surface waves along the flat impedance flange exited by semi-infinite waveguide was carried out. The solution of problem was conducted using variation principle in the single-mode approach. Considering a semi-infinite cylindrical waveguide of arbitrary cross section, it is possible to build integral equation in the linear combination of the tangential components of electrical and magnetic field on the waveguide aperture. Formulas for calculation the surface wave excitation coefficient and radiation pattern of surface wave were obtainedasing variation principle. The numerical analysis of the surface waves characteristics exited along the impedance flange by coaxial and circular waveguides was conducted on the basis of obtained formulas.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Investigation of periodic and quasi-periodic layered artificial structure (bianisotropic-isotropic layers)
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this work multilayered periodic structures including bianisotropic and isotropic layers are studied. A bianisotropy axis direction and a wave propagation direction are chosen to be arbitrary. The analytical approach of investigation of such structures based on the translation matrix method is used. It is obtained that all four eigeonumbers of this is different. Therefore there are four different eigenwave in the periodic structure.

articleTitle: The numerical analysis of processes of resonant scattering of intensive electromagnetic fields on the nonlinear dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: On an example of the open nonlinear electrodynamic system - transverse non-homogeneous, isotropic, nonmagnetic, linearly polarized, nonlinear (a Kerr-like dielectric nonlinearity) dielectric layer, the algorithm of solution of the nonlinear diffraction problem and the results of the numerical analysis are shown. Are found out: effect of non-uniform shift of resonant frequency and effect of increase of the angle of the transparency of the nonlinear layer at growth of intensity of the field.

publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.

articleTitle: Resonant excitation of plasma oscillations in a two-dimensional electron layer via diffraction of the electromagnetic wave on a perfectly conductive gate electrode
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: In this paper, we solve the problem of excitation of plasma oscillations in 2D electron layer selfconsistently using the full system of the Maxwell equations. We formulate this problem as the problem of diffraction of the incoming plane electromagnetic wave on a gate electrode.

articleTitle: Perforated strips as rejection FSS
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: The total reflection resonances that take place at the excitation of a grating of perforated strips with one aperture over the period are discussed. Such a grating provides rejection frequency response. If appropriate dimensions of the slots are chosen, such a simple FSS provides high qualily-factor rejection resonance of the required frequency. Numerical results concerning frequency and angle dependences for the perforated strip are presented. Strict conformity between the rejection resonances in perforated strip and rejection waveguide irises is confirmed.

articleTitle: A way to taking into account fluctuations in superfluorescence in the Dicke model
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Kinetics of emitters interacting with equilibrium photon field has been studied with taking into account nonequilibrium fluctuations in the subsystem, of emitters. The consideration is based on the Bogolyubov reduced description method applied to the basic kinetic equation for the statistical operator of the emitters. The general stochastic approach is applied to construct kinetic equations for the system with nonequilibrium correlations.

articleTitle: Dyadic Green's function for shielded planar line analysis
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Electric type dyadic Green's function is derived for the full-wave analysis of shielded planar transmission line configurations. Green's dyadic components of a multilayered region are presented as a series expansion over a complete set of Helmholtz operator eigenfunctions with one-dimensional Green's functions as unknown coefficients. For the Green's functions analytically simple and uniform expressions are obtained. The Green's dyadic of the multilayered region is involved in the electric field integral formulation for overlapping reginus to construct a generalized Computational algorithm for the analysis of planar transmission lines. To validate the presented approach, several shielded planar line configurations, such as hroadside-coupled microstrip lines, bilateral finlines, and hroadside-coupled coplanar waveguides, are analyzed and calculation results are compared with available data.

articleTitle: Analyzing the effects of conductive and permeable soil on the EMI response for UXO discrimination
publicationTitle: 10th International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory, 2004.
abstract: Unexploded ordinances (UXO) are buried typically in the top 1 m of soil. Low frequency (from tens of Hertz up to several hundreds of kHertz) electromagnetic induction (EMI) sensing has been identified as one of most promising technology for UXO detection as well for discrimination. They use the principle of EM1 in which unseen object are detected by sensing eddy current induced in metal by a primary magnetic field. It is known that the EMI sensors are sensitive to the scatters electromagnetic parameters (conductivity and permeability). Therefore, in this paper, low frequency scattering from a highly conducting and permeable metallic objects buried in geological soil are exposed and analyzed from the unexploded ordnances (UXO) detection and discrimination point of new. The method of auxiliary sources (MAS) in conjunction with thin skin approximation (TSA) is used for understanding physics of electromagnetic induction (EMI) scattering phenomena. Several numerical examples are designed to show how the geological soil's electromagnetic parameters (conductivity and permeability) affect object's EMI response.

abstract: A variational method for solution of the nonlinear vector spectral problem for the case of linear self-adjoint positively semi-definite operators functioning in real Hilbertian spaces with nonlinearly included spectral parameters, is stated in the report. Such problems arise, in particular, at studying the solutions to the problems of nonlinear radiating systems synthesis.
